title: Pocket-sized drug discovery: An AI-empowered smartphone platform coupled with single-atom nanozymes for on-site inhibitor screening.
abstract: The point-of-care (POC) quantification of α-glucosidase (α-Glu) activity and the high-throughput screening of its inhibitors are pivotal for antidiabetic drug discovery, yet they are frequently hindered by the reliance on bulky optical instruments and unstable colorimetric systems. Herein, this work reported an integrated "pocket-sized" analytical platform synergizing an ionic liquid (IL)-regulated Co-N-C single-atom nanozyme (SAzyme) with artificial intelligence (AI)-empowered smartphone analytics. Synthesized via IL-mediated cobalt anchoring and pyrolysis, the engineered SAzyme featured an optimized coordination microenvironment that exhibits robust, H2O2-free oxidase-like activity. This catalyzed the oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB), driving a highly specific target-triggered cascade: α-Glu hydrolyzes α-arbutin to yield hydroquinone, triggering a naked-eye visible "signal-off" reductive fading (limit of detection [LOD] = 0.106 U/L). Conversely, inhibitors block this cascade, preserving the blue signal to elegantly translate the inhibition into a distinct "signal-on" readout. To bridge the gap between benchtop precision and on-site deployment, a smartphone-assisted RGB chromaticity analysis was implemented, achieving a reliable instrument-free LOD of 0.645 U/L. Building upon this, a custom-built smartphone application was constructed to autonomously extract multidimensional color features. By embedding a multilayer perceptron (MLP) algorithm, the platform accurately interpreted these optical signals to predict α-Glu activity (validation R2 = 0.927). Utilizing this all-in-one system, the high-throughput POC screening of natural compounds was successfully executed, identifying ursolic acid (IC50 = 3.43 μM) and glycyrrhetinic acid (IC50 = 13.01 μM) as potent inhibitors. Ultimately, this work delivered a versatile, highly integrated approach that liberates enzymatic assays from laboratory constraints, offering a robust strategy for advanced biomedical sensing and drug discovery.

title: Exploiting temporal information in higher-order fluorescence data for enhanced pattern recognition: Application to saffron geographical authentication.
abstract: Recent studies using fluorescence data have demonstrated that incorporating additional experimental modes can provide valuable discriminatory information. However, the discriminant value of higher-order data may depend not only on the information acquired, but also on how it is extracted and represented before classification. Here, an in-flow photodegradation strategy was developed to generate time-resolved EEM fluorescence data from saffron extracts. Different data structures were evaluated for saffron geographical authentication. Following PARAFAC decomposition, the resulting latent variables were used as inputs for supervised and one-class classification approaches to assess whether preserving sample-specific temporal fluorescence evolution improves pattern recognition performance. Three data structures were evaluated: second-order/three-way, third-order/four-way, and third-order/augmented three-way. PARAFAC decomposition was performed for each structure, and the resulting scores were used as input variables for supervised and one-class classification. In supervised classification using a backpropagation neural network, all three data structures provided good discrimination among saffron geographical classes. However, differences between data representations became more pronounced when DD-SIMCA was applied. All three models achieved 100 % sensitivity for the target class, whereas the percentage of correctly rejected non-target samples increased from 68 % for the second-order/three-way data to 86 % for the third-order/four-way data and 100 % for the augmented three-way data. These results demonstrate that the improvement from higher-order data is not solely due to incorporating an additional temporal dimension, but also to how temporal information is retained in the PARAFAC score matrix and subsequently transferred to the classification model. This study demonstrates that data representation is a critical factor when exploiting higher-order fluorescence information. Although all data structures provided good supervised discrimination, preserving sample-specific temporal evolution substantially improved one-class classification. The results highlight the importance of designing dimensionality-reduction strategies that retain system-specific information relevant to class discrimination.

title: Simultaneous dynamic spectrophotometric determination of coexisting rare earth elements in acidic chloride media using response-specific multivariate calibration.
abstract: Reliable spectrophotometric determination of coexisting rare-earth elements in strongly acidic chloride media remains analytically challenging because of weak 4f-4f absorption responses, severe spectral overlap, and baseline instability under dynamic measurement conditions. This study presents a dynamic absorption spectroscopic method coupled with a response-specific multi-scale peak-basis linear regression model (RS-MPBLR) for continuous in situ quantification of Nd3+ and Pr3+ in strongly acidic coexisting systems relevant to NdFeB magnet recycling. Characteristic absorption peaks, multi-scale spectral descriptors, and derivative-related features were integrated to enhance response specificity and robustness against spectral overlap, acidity-dependent background variation, and flow-induced baseline drift. Spectral analysis confirmed an approximately linear absorbance-concentration relationship within the investigated range, supporting peak-oriented linear modeling. RS-MPBLR was evaluated using leave-one-concentration-out cross-validation and benchmarked against partial least squares, principal component regression, and ridge regression, achieving lower prediction errors and more stable error distributions. Dynamic online experiments demonstrated continuous tracking of stepwise concentration changes, with R2 values above 0.97 and limits of detection of 0.07 and 0.03 g/L for Nd3+ and Pr3+, respectively. Cross-day segment-wise analysis further confirmed stable online predictions, with coefficients of variation mostly below 1-2% and σpred values within 0.015-0.040 g/L for Nd3+ and 0.006-0.021 g/L for Pr3+. This study provides a robust and sensitive spectrophotometric soft-sensing strategy for continuous rare-earth ion quantification in hydrochloric acid media. By combining response-specific modeling with reference-sample-based calibration correction, it overcomes the difficulty of long-term dynamic detection under online flowing conditions and enables reliable quantification for NdFeB magnet hydrometallurgical recycling.

title: Simultaneous quantification of gold and silver nanoparticles in spiked buffered river surface water using fluorescence spectroscopy and U-PLS/RBL.
abstract: The accelerated production and use of engineered nanoparticles in commercial products will inevitably result in their release into aquatic environments, raising concerns about potential ecological and health impacts. Distinguishing synthetic nanomaterials from naturally occurring colloids in environmental samples remains a major analytical challenge because of matrix complexity and the coexistence of multiple nanoparticle types with diverse sizes, shapes, and surface chemistries. In this study, we present a second-order multivariate calibration strategy based on unfolded partial least squares coupled with residual bilinearization (U-PLS/RBL) for the simultaneous quantification of gold nanoparticles and silver nanoparticles in water samples. Fluorescence excitation-emission matrices were recorded using rhodamine 6G and a carbazole derivative as fluorescent probes. The quenching effects induced by the nanoparticles were used to construct quenching matrices, which were then analyzed by U-PLS/RBL. The proposed methodology achieved low detection limits in the picomolar range, high sensitivity, and excellent recovery (92-110%) in both river surface water and tap water samples, without requiring prior separation or pretreatment. These results highlight the robustness and cost-effectiveness of U-PLS/RBL for nanoparticle analysis and demonstrate its potential as a valuable tool for environmental monitoring of engineered nanomaterials.

title: Vibrational spectroscopy of microorganisms: A review.
abstract: Vibrational spectroscopic methods, mid- and near-infrared, and Raman spectroscopies, have been extensively applied to the study of microorganisms. This is due to the relatively rapid analysis time, relative low-cost, experimental flexibility, and phenotypic nature of these methods. Consequently, vibrational spectroscopies have been investigated for clinical, environmental and industrial microbiology applications. This review outlines the principles of mid- and near-infrared, and Raman spectroscopies, and steps through vibrational spectroscopic experiments in the context of microbiological studies. Further applications within species/strain identification, antimicrobial resistance, bioremediation, cell sorting and intracellular microbial protein analysis are examined. Vibrational spectroscopy is expected to become increasingly routine in microbial analyses, particularly in clinical settings, driven by the harmonisation of spectral databases, the expanding application of deep learning methods and improved instrumentation to reduce sampling-to-reporting time.

title: Integrated multi-omics, network pharmacology, and machine learning reveal the active constituents and pharmacological mechanism of Fufang E'jiao Jiang against lung cancer-related fatigue.
abstract: Fufang E'jiao Jiang (FEJ), a classic traditional Chinese medicine formula for improving immunity, has demonstrated clinical efficacy in alleviating lung cancer-related fatigue (LCRF). FEJ contains both plant-derived herbs and animal-derived donkey-hide gelatin, yet its complex chemical composition-particularly the collagen-derived peptides and proteins-remains incompletely characterized. However, a systematic characterization of its complex chemical composition remains lacking, and the underlying anti-LCRF mechanism of its are yet to be fully elucidated. By integrating metabolomics (UHPLC-QTOF-MS and GC-MS), peptidomics, and proteomics (NanoLC-Orbitrap-MS/MS), we identified 186 small molecules, 243 peptides, and 42 proteins in FEJ, substantially expanding the chemical coverage relative to previous reports that focused mainly on small molecules. Notably, collagen-derived peptides and proteins from donkey-hide gelatin were characterized for the first time. Network pharmacology and consensus machine learning (LASSO, random forest, and SVM-RFE) prioritized 17 potential key constituents (including 8 donkey-hide gelatin peptides, 5 ginsenosides, and others), spanning all five constituent medicinal materials. Six core targets (IL1B, IL6, TNF, MTOR, BCL2L1, and BDNF) were screened and were predicted to be associated with the regulation of inflammation, energy metabolism, and skeletal muscle function, potentially through the NF-κB and PI3K-Akt signaling pathways. The main novelty lies in the first comprehensive characterization of FEJ including peptides and proteins, and in the establishment of a multi-omics workflow applicable to animal-containing traditional Chinese medicine formulas. These findings provide a solid chemical basis for deciphering the anti-LCRF mechanisms of FEJ and warrant further experimental validation.

title: Multiscale adaptive graph attention band selection for hyperspectral rosewood species classification.
abstract: The identification of precious timber represented by national standard Rosewood remains challenged by the time-intensive and destructive nature of conventional approaches. Hyperspectral imaging offers a non-destructive alternative, yet its application is hindered by high dimensionality and spectral redundancy. Existing methods often struggle to simultaneously capture global spectral dependencies and localized chemical features. This study presents an integrated framework combining a multiscale adaptive graph attention-based band selection method with stability consistency (MAGABSS-SC) and a dual-domain resonant state space network (D2R-S2Net). MAGABSS-SC employs supervised multiscale attention and PageRank propagation to identify topologically robust bands, which are directly fed into D2R-S2Net to integrate frequency-domain filtering with temporal state space sequence modeling. Evaluated on a hyperspectral dataset of eighteen Rosewood species comprising 1800 spectral samples, D2R-S2Net achieved an accuracy of 93.33% using full-band input, outperforming support vector machines, random forests, and one-dimensional vision transformers. When combined with MAGABSS-SC, the classification accuracy reached 95.93% while retaining 80% of the spectral bands. The selected wavelengths exhibited contiguous cluster distributions aligned with general absorption intervals reported in wood spectroscopy literature. The proposed framework provides an accurate and non-destructive approach for the classification of endangered rosewood species. By mitigating spectral redundancy and noise interference, it demonstrates the feasibility of combining graph-based band selection with dual-domain deep learning for timber identification and forest resource regulation.

title: Antifouling superhydrophilic hydrogel-based electrochemical sensor for robust multi-analyte sweat analysis.
abstract: Reliable sweat analysis in complex biological environments remains challenging due to biofouling-induced signal degradation and analyte interference. Herein, a superhydrophilic antifouling hydrogel-based electrochemical sensor is developed by integrating TiO2-decorated MXene (MXene@TiO2) into a borax-crosslinked PVA network for intelligent multi-analyte sweat analysis. The MXene@TiO2 not only provides conductivity and electrocatalytic activity, but also enhances hydrophilicity of the sensing interface, thereby suppressing nonspecific protein adsorption. The sensor enables sensitive and selective detection of dopamine, uric acid, and ascorbic acid, with detection limits as low as 0.0491, 0.1187, and 0.2451 μM, respectively. Under protein-interference conditions containing 10 mg mL-1 bovine serum albumin (BSA), the current attenuation for DA, UA, and AA was limited to 24.88%, 13.37%, and 12.65%, respectively, demonstrating resistance to biofouling-induced signal loss. Machine-learning-based classification and regression were further employed for analyte identification and concentration prediction, achieving a classification accuracy of 97.9% and an R2 of 0.978 for concentration prediction. Furthermore, a wearable sensing platform incorporating wireless communication and mobile-based data processing enables wearable signal acquisition and intelligent analysis, while droplet-based validation yielded recoveries from 99.45% to 100.80%. By integrating superhydrophilic antifouling interface engineering with machine-learning-assisted signal interpretation, this work provides a robust strategy for intelligent multi-analyte sweat sensing and wearable health monitoring.

title: Eutectogel-based thin film microextraction coupled with UPLC-PDA for selective detection of diflufenican.
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) pesticides remain an under-quantified source of human dietary exposure, largely due to their trace-level occurrence and the complexity of food matrices. These analytical challenges underscore the need for selective extraction approaches capable of minimizing matrix interferences. In this work, a new thin-film microextraction (TFME) device incorporating multifunctional eutectogels was developed for the selective extraction and preconcentration of the PFAS herbicide diflufenican from food samples prior to UPLC-PDA quantification, and its performance was systematically evaluated. High-throughput screening of selectivity-enhanced deep eutectic solvents (DESs) toward diflufenican was performed using machine-learning-enhanced quantum chemical methods. Simultaneously, the eutectogel-based thin film was fabricated via UV-initiated photopolymerization of the DES, monomer, and crosslinker, yielding supramolecular gels stabilized by non-covalent interactions. The established method demonstrated excellent analytical performance, with a wide linear range (0.5-500 μg/L), a low LOD (0.04 μg/L and 0.53 μg/kg), and satisfactory recoveries (97.2-112%). Compared with the established methods, the proposed method possessed higher precision while affording a lower limit of detection and reduced hazardous reagent consumption. Mechanistic exploration corroborated by molecular simulations and multi-spectroscopic characterizations revealed that the eutectogel effectively captures diflufenican through hydrogen-bond interaction, π-π transpose, and proton-transfer inhibition, while the original DES interaction network undergoes dynamic reorganization. The demonstrated tunability of the developed eutectogel-based thin-film microextraction device positions it as a versatile platform for the selective preconcentration of fluorinated species in complex matrices, supporting advances in the monitoring of hazardous substances in food.

title: Lysosome-targeted fluorescent probe for real-time imaging of hypochlorite in rheumatoid arthritis and machine learning-assisted quantification in plant tissues.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease closely associated with excessive oxidative stress. Hypochlorite (ClO-) are key reactive oxidants in inflammatory microenvironments which contribute to lysosomal dysfunction and inflammatory cascade amplification. However, rapid and selective visualization of ClO- in complex biological systems remains challenging. In addition, residual ClO- in plant-derived foods raises safety concerns, while conventional analytical methods are unsuitable for direct in situ detection. To address this issue, we developed a lysosome-targeted fluorescent probe HB-Z, for sensitive ClO- detection in RA models and plant tissues. The designed probe HB-Z consists of a 1,8-naphthalimide-based fluorophore, p-aminophenyl ether recognition unit, and morpholine lysosomal-targeting group, enabling remarkable turn-on fluorescence response upon ClO- triggered cleavage. Spectroscopic studies demonstrated excellent selectivity, rapid response within seconds, high sensitivity, and good pH stability. HB-Z successfully imaged exogenous and endogenous ClO- in live RAW 264.7 macrophages with distinct lysosomal localization. In a λ-carrageenan-induced acute arthritis mouse model, HB-Z enabled visualization of elevated joint ClO- levels and real-time monitoring of oxidative fluctuations during disease progression and antioxidant-mediated remission. Furthermore, HB-Z achieved concentration-dependent fluorescence imaging of exogenous ClO- residues in soybean sprouts. By integrating fluorescence features and soaking time, a stochastic gradient descent machine-learning classifier further enabled three-class discrimination of disinfection status with high accuracy. This probe provides a versatile platform for dynamic ClO- imaging in inflammatory diseases and intelligent assessment of food disinfection quality, possessing great potential for exploring the mechanism of inflammatory diseases and realizing intelligent food safety detection.

title: A comparison of PCA, ASCA, and vASCA for enhancing the interpretability of biological Raman spectroscopy.
abstract: Raman spectroscopy is often used to analyze complex biological systems, but interpreting the resulting spectra remains difficult because of overlapping vibrational bands and the limitations of standard multivariate approaches such as Principal Component Analysis. This work assesses whether ANOVA-Simultaneous Component Analysis and its variable-selection extension can address these interpretability issues. More specifically, the goal was to determine if this approach could isolate spectral features that reflect metabolic syndrome and its progression over time. Serum Raman spectra were collected from control rats and those with metabolic syndrome at four time points. The datasets were then analyzed comparatively using Principal Component Analysis, ANOVA-Simultaneous Component Analysis, and Variable-Selection ANOVA-Simultaneous Component Analysis, with attention not only to statistical separation but also to the interpretability of the resulting features in a biochemical context. Variable-Selection ANOVA-Simultaneous Component Analysis shows a narrower set of statistically relevant spectral regions. Among these, a Raman band in the 907-926 cm-1 range appeared as a candidate signature associated with metabolic syndrome. Temporal variation was also evident, particularly in lipid- and protein-related bands between 8 and 52 weeks, although some overlap across groups persisted. Compared with the other methods, this approach yielded a clearer feature-based separation and, in most comparisons, stronger statistical contrasts. The use of Variable-Selection ANOVA-Simultaneous Component Analysis makes the relationship between spectral features and the physiology of the disease clearer. Our approach paves the way to establish an interpretable tool to identify relevant spectral signatures in biological Raman spectra datasets.

title: Machine learning-assisted fluorescence immunochromatographic detection of Salmonella typhimurium in complex food matrices via tannic acid-enhanced AIE nanoprobes.
abstract: Rapid on-site detection of Salmonella typhimurium in complex food matrices remains challenging due to the need for fluorescent probes that maintain intense emission in aqueous environments while resisting interference from salts and pH fluctuations. In this work, we explore tannic acid (TA) as a non-covalent interfacial modifier to construct SiO2/TCPE/TA (STT) nanoparticles for fluorescence immunochromatographic assays (ICA). Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations reveal that TA interacts with the aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) TCPE through cooperative π-π stacking and hydrogen bonding, which stabilizes the excited state, slightly narrows the energy gap, and suppresses non-radiative decay pathways. Guided by the theoretical predictions, we synthesize STT nanoparticles featuring uniform spherical morphology, tunable size, and a TA-enriched surface. The TA modification boosts the absolute fluorescence quantum yield from 12.91% to 30.51% and extends the fluorescence lifetime from 1.79 ns to 2.57 ns. Taking advantage of these improved photophysical properties, the STT-based ICA strip achieves a visual detection limit of 500 CFU mL-1 and a quantitative limit of 128 CFU mL-1 for S. typhimurium. Practical applicability is confirmed in spiked milk, chicken, and lettuce samples, with recoveries ranging from 82.75% to 119.29%. Moreover, a machine-learning classifier trained on strip images from the three food matrices attains perfect classification accuracy across five concentration levels, enabling automated and objective result reading. This work presents a non-covalent confinement strategy to engineer bright and robust AIE nanoprobes. By combining mechanistic insights from DFT calculations with experimental validation, the TA-mediated approach not only enhances fluorescence performance but also ensures matrix tolerance. The successful integration of STT nanoparticles into a lateral flow immunoassay, coupled with machine-learning-assisted interpretation, offers a rapid, sensitive, and user-friendly platform for foodborne pathogen surveillance, with strong potential for point-of-need applications.

title: A fluorescent optical platform sensor based on ratiometric carbon dots integrated with machine learning for the identification and detection of organic solvents.
abstract: Rapid identification of organic solvents is of great significance for chemical analysis, environmental monitoring and laboratory safety. In this study, ratiometric carbon dots (R-CDs) were integrated with machine learning to develop a portable fluorescence-based optical sensing platform for the rapid discrimination and recognition of common organic solvents. Based on the highly sensitive solvatochromic response of R-CDs fluorescence intensity ratio (I590nm/I502nm), a six-channel sensor array was constructed by preparing water/organic-solvent mixtures with different solvent fractions. And owing to the distinct fluorescence responses of R-CDs in solvents with different Relative Polarity (ETN) values, principal component analysis (PCA), hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA) and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) were employed to discriminate and identify five organic solvents with ETN values ranging from 0.355 to 0.762. Specifically, PCA and HCA were used for label-free analysis of the fluorescence signals, while LDA was employed for model training and prediction. Furthermore, by combining the optical sensing platform with self-developed computer software, a multifunctional system capable of solvent detection, recognition, and result visualization was established. The results showed that five organic solvents could be successfully distinguished with an identification accuracy of 100%, demonstrating the promising potential of the proposed optical sensing platform for organic solvent recognition.

title: SERS ratiometric strategy leveraging carbon allocation trade-off enables Tremella fuciformis metabolic phenotyping and traceability.
abstract: Accurate metabolic phenotyping and geographical traceability of gelatinous fungi are critical for uncovering fungal physiological adaptation mechanisms and advancing edible fungus quality supervision. However, high phenotypic similarity and subtle metabolic differences in homologous fungal samples pose formidable challenges to conventional physicochemical assays. Especially, relying on chemical fingerprinting without biological phenotypic implications, conventional surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) analysis is unable to discern delicate metabolic discrepancies in fungal samples. Herein, we propose a metabolic characteristic peak ratio-based SERS strategy using Tremella fuciformis (T. fuciformis) as the model. By extracting intrinsic metabolic signatures represented by the carbon allocation trade-off between stress-resistant functional polysaccharides and storage-type carbohydrates, it delivers metabolic specificity and detection stability/reproducibility that are not possible with traditional fingerprint-based SERS fungal analysis. Integrated with machine learning, this method accurately differentiates six T. fuciformis samples, including specimens with distinct metabolic phenotypes as well as geographically differentiated samples with highly similar phenotypic features, achieving a superior accuracy of 99.2% and an AUC of 1.0. Combined with a custom-built portable Raman device we constructed, the entire detection procedure can be completed within 15 min, enabling efficient on-site analysis. This study establishes a bio-signature-oriented SERS paradigm that upgrades chemical fingerprint identification to fungal metabolic phenotyping, providing a versatile technical platform for exploring fungal metabolic variation and phenotypic differentiation.

title: Quantitative analysis of heavy metals in ores by X-ray fluorescence with improved CARS and support vector regression using ACOR optimization algorithm.
abstract: X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectrometry is widely applied for the quantitative determination of elemental concentrations in ores due to its rapid, non-destructive, and multi-element analytical capabilities. However, the high dimensionality, spectral redundancy, and strong matrix-dependent nonlinear effects inherent in XRF spectra often limit the predictive accuracy and robustness of conventional quantitative models. Therefore, the effective selection of informative spectral variables and the construction of reliable regression models remain critical challenges for accurate ore analysis. In this study, an integrated quantitative framework combining adaptive heuristic optimization and machine-learning regression is proposed to improve elemental concentration prediction from ore XRF spectra. First, a competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (CARS) strategy optimized by the ant colony optimization for continuous domains (ACOR) algorithm is employed to perform robust spectral variable selection. This process removes redundant noisy spectral information while preserving chemically relevant features. Subsequently, an ACOR-optimized support vector regression (ACOR-SVR) model is developed for quantitative analysis. In this model, key SVR hyperparameters are automatically tuned to enhance nonlinear modelling capability and improve generalization performance. The proposed ACSVR framework is evaluated on multi-element ore datasets involving Fe, Cu, Zn, and Pb. The experimental results demonstrate that ACOR-CARS provides more stable and compact feature subsets than conventional CARS, whereas ACOR-SVR consistently outperforms baseline SVR and other classical machine-learning models. High prediction accuracy is achieved for Fe, Cu, Zn, and Pb, with coefficients of determination (R2) reaching 0.9940, 0.9984, 0.9968, and 0.9995, respectively. These results confirm the effectiveness of integrating optimized variable selection with nonlinear regression modelling for XRF-based quantitative analyses. Overall, this study provides a practical and efficient strategy for high-precision elemental quantification in ores, offering strong potential for mineral exploration, resource evaluation and intelligent geochemical analysis.

title: Decoding in-situ plant stress physiology via bio-hydrogel microneedles.
abstract: Electrochemical detection of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) dynamics enables early monitoring of plant stress physiology, which is crucial for crop health management and yield optimization. However, invasive sensors damage plant tissues, whereas existing non-invasive approaches suffer from cuticular barriers and insufficient exploitation of dynamic biochemical signals, leading to high interfacial impedance, delayed responses, and low accuracy. Here, we introduce an integrated sensing and machine-learning framework (CRH-BMIS) that combines a highly specific Cs/rGO/HRP biohydrogel microneedle with algorithmic analytics. This system overcomes traditional barriers to in situ, tissue-level monitoring of abiotic and Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 (Pst DC3000) stresses. By significantly lowering interfacial impedance, the microneedle exhibits a stable log-linear response over an ultra-broad range (0.01-8000 μM) with exceptional sensitivity (up to 12.46 μA cm-2 decade-1, LOD 0.00109 μM) and robust anti-interference. Furthermore, utilizing an intelligent diagnostic model based on stress-evoked H2O2 dynamics, CRH-BMIS achieves competitive cross-plant classification of abiotic/biotic stress (96.97% accuracy) and disease-stage classification (91.47% accuracy). This superior performance stems from the deep synergy between minimally invasive microneedles and machine learning algorithms. CRH-BMIS not only delivers accurate, generalizable in situ stress diagnosis but also enables scalable early-warning decision support.

title: An electrochemical sensor platform for rapid nucleic acid detection of Influenza A in unamplified samples and machine-learning-assisted infection diagnosis.
abstract: Influenza A remains a major cause of respiratory infection that demands for rapid, accurate and readily accessible diagnostic tools for timely clinical decision-making and outbreak control. Here, we report a smartphone-assisted electrochemical biosensor platform for amplification-free nucleic acid detection of Influenza A based on magnetic beads enriched target capture and methylene blue (MB)-mediated signal transduction. Under optimized conditions, the platform enabled sensitive detection of both synthetic complementary DNA and RNA, with limits of detection of 0.33aM and 3.32aM, respectively, while maintaining high selectivity against mismatched and non-target sequences. Additionally, the platform is also applied to the detection of RNA extracted from nasopharyngeal swab samples and shows superior discrimination ability between positive and negative samples as well as strong correlation with reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) results. Finally, an optimal machine-learning framework based on a support vector classifier (SVC) is developed to analyze DPV signal profiles and directly classify clinical samples without explicit comparison to blank-current responses, achieving an accuracy of 100% in the clinical cohort. Unlike conventional nucleic acid detection approaches that mainly rely on predefined thresholds or quantitative signal interpretation, this study establishes a machine-learning-assisted classification strategy for direct discrimination of influenza A nucleic-acid positive and negative samples based on electrochemical DPV signal profiles. This simple algorithmic framework is particularly suitable for portable devices with resource constrained microcontrollers to realize rapid result analysis. Our results shed a light on potential portable platform for decentralized rapid nucleic acid testing and promising technique for point-of-care infectious disease diagnostics.

title: Discovery of thiol-reactive Staphylococcus aureus sortase A inhibitors from natural products by machine learning and thiocholine mass-shift profiling.
abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) remains a major clinical challenge, and Sortase A (SrtA), a cysteine transpeptidase involved in surface-protein anchoring and biofilm formation, represents an attractive anti-virulence target. In this study, we developed an integrated analytical workflow combining machine-learning (ML)-guided taxon prioritisation, affinity magnetic capture, mass-shift profiling, and biochemical target-engagement assays to identify natural-product SrtA inhibitors from complex botanical extracts. A random-forest classifier trained on ChEMBL SrtA bioactivity data was applied to the LOTUS natural-product database to prioritise Michael-acceptor-containing botanical sources, leading to the selection of Piper retrofractum for constituent-level analysis. Subsequent chemical profiling and affinity-capture experiments identified piperlongumine as a thiol-reactive constituent preferentially associated with active SrtA. Piperlongumine inhibited SrtA transpeptidase activity with an IC50 of 27.83 ± 1.04 μmol/L and showed a higher TCI-adduct response and stronger SrtA inhibition than the structurally related alkaloid piperine. Time-dependent enzyme inhibition, competitive 5-FAM-LPETG bead imaging, and mPEG-maleimide thiol-occupancy analysis further supported thiol-dependent SrtA engagement under the assay conditions. Piperlongumine also inhibited biofilm formation across multiple S. aureus strains while exerting limited effects on planktonic growth at corresponding concentrations. These findings demonstrate an analytical strategy that links computational prioritisation, crude-extract chemical profiling, affinity capture, and target-engagement validation for the discovery of thiol-reactive natural products targeting SrtA.

title: Mislabeling (label noise) - an often overlooked issue in chemometrics.
abstract: In supervised learning, errors can arise in label values. This fact is well known in machine learning (ML), where it has been studied since the late 1960s, but is often ignored in chemometrics. The main reason for mislabeling is human errors when supervision is carried out by a person. It is also inevitable in cases where a continuous process is divided into stages for their subsequent supervised discrimination. Another reason is the imperfection of an instrumental method, which poorly reflects the differences between classes. This paper pursues two goals. The first one is to introduce the concept of mislabeling in chemometrics. The second goal is to share our experience in solving mislabeling problems that arise in real-world examples. In our opinion, the most appropriate approach is the integration of the domain knowledge with the outlier detection methods, which should be based on probabilistic (soft) classifiers. This approach is used systematically and is illustrated by three cases that employ both well-established and new methods. Mislabeling is a real problem that can occur across a variety of applications, reaching up to 20%, and in some areas, such as medicine, this rate can be even higher. There is no doubt that mislabeling deserves investigation and correction. In mission-critical fields, particularly in medicine, the cost of an error caused by mislabeled data can be significant, measured not only in financial losses but also in human lives.

title: Deep learning-based excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopic analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in coal tar.
abstract: Rapid and accurate analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in coal tar (CT) is essential yet challenging due to spectral overlap and matrix effects. Excitation-emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectral analysis using deep learning algorithms can address this challenge. Coal tar samples were extracted and diluted with cyclohexane. A dataset of 1173 EEM spectra covering 3- to 6-ring PAHs and various concentration gradients was constructed. Seven machine learning algorithms were used for qualitative classification of PAHs, and the deep learning algorithm, ResNet18, achieved the highest accuracy, close to 90%. Quantitative analysis was performed using a convolutional neural network-based variational autoencoder (CNN-VAE) model, yielding Root mean square error (RMSE) and (Mean absolute error) MAE values as low as 0.0036 mg/L and 0.0028 mg/L, respectively. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for accurate PAH quantification in complex coal-tar matrices. This new approach provides a cost-effective, rapid, and reliable alternative to conventional methods, mitigating issues such as Rayleigh scattering and spectral overlap. It offers a new strategy for detecting PAH molecules in complex matrices.

title: Why choose between prediction power and mechanistic insight in QSRR modeling? A case study of artificial membrane chromatography and machine learning.
abstract: Quantitative structure-retention relationship (QSRR) modeling of immobilized artificial membrane (IAM) chromatography was performed on a chemically diverse set of 2003 analytes to determine whether mechanistically interpretable, descriptor-based models can match the predictive performance of advanced machine-learning approaches. Chromatographic hydrophobicity indices (CHIIAM) were measured under standardized fast-gradient IAM conditions and modeled using three molecular representation strategies: physicochemical descriptors, ECFP4 fingerprints, and a Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN) operating on molecular graphs. Among the descriptor- and fingerprint-based methods, the Gradient Boosting Regressor gave the best performance. The descriptor-based model achieved a test R2 of 0.817, MAE of 4.43, and RMSE of 6.46 CHIIAM units, whereas the GIN model showed only a marginal numerical improvement (R2 = 0.828, MAE = 4.27, RMSE = 6.25). In contrast, fingerprint-based modeling performed worse (R2 = 0.771, MAE = 5.04, RMSE = 7.22). Statistical analysis of paired prediction errors showed no significant difference between the descriptor-based and GIN models, while the fingerprint-based model was the least accurate of the three. The observed differences among the best models were smaller than the long-term reproducibility of the IAM protocol. Applicability-domain analysis further showed that approximately 94-99% of compounds fell within the interpolation region. SHAP analysis identified lipophilicity, ionization, charge, and polarity as the major determinants of IAM retention, with cationic character enhancing retention and high polarity reducing it. These results demonstrate that descriptor-based QSRR modeling can achieve near-deep learning performance while preserving mechanistic interpretability, providing a practical and physically grounded strategy for IAM retention prediction.

title: Machine learning-assisted fluorescent sensor array based on siloxane-derived porous polymers for high-throughput discrimination of multiple antibiotics in milk.
abstract: Both simultaneous monitoring of multiple antibiotic residues for public health security and accurate single-analyte quantification for regulatory compliance are critically important, though the former remains challenging due to structural diversity among analytes. Herein, we constructed a four-channel fluorescent sensor array based on siloxane-derived porous polymers for discriminative detection of 12 antibiotics spanning four categories (chloramphenicols, nitrofurans, nitroimidazoles, and tetracyclines), and further achieved discrimination of 6 antibiotics in real milk samples at lower concentrations (0.5 μM), along with quantitative determination of oxytetracycline (OTC) in two brands of milk. The array primarily generates differential fluorescence responses through synergistic inner filter effects and photoinduced electron transfer, featuring rapid response (<15 s), high sensitivity (detection limit down to 0.16 μM), and excellent recyclability (POSS-Ph exhibits > 90% fluorescence retention for tetracycline (TC) after 5 consecutive cycles). Integrated with machine learning algorithms (e.g., LDA and KNN), the sensor achieved 100% identification accuracy in spiked milk samples, demonstrating its potential as a robust platform for high-throughput antibiotic screening in complex matrices.

title: SpectralTAG: Functional group identification from infrared spectra via unified LLM and GNN textual graphs.
abstract: Spectral analysis underpins much of modern chemical characterization, yet extracting chemically meaningful interpretations from spectral signals remains constrained by the disconnect between data-driven pattern recognition and structured domain knowledge. Here we present SpectralTAG, a unified graph-based reasoning framework that bridges this gap by representing infrared spectra, hierarchical chemical knowledge graphs, and scientific text within a common textual attribute graph (TAG). In this representation, continuous spectra are discretized into semantically annotated range nodes, aligned with functional-group and vibration-type entities from a chemical ontology, and augmented with task-specific prompt and response nodes, enabling a single graph backbone to support node-level functional group classification, edge-level peak-pair relationship judgment, and graph-level molecular classification tasks through large language model encoding and graph neural network inference, without task-specific architectural redesign. Evaluated on 306 organic molecules with infrared spectra, SpectralTAG achieves AUC > 0.98 on edge- and graph-level tasks across 24 encoder-GNN combinations, with LLaMa2-7b paired with R-GCN delivering the most consistent cross-task performance. The framework further supports multitask training with negligible performance trade-off and exhibits emerging zero-shot and few-shot generalization under disjoint label conditions. These results establish textual attribute graphs as a viable paradigm for unifying heterogeneous scientific data within a single reasoning architecture, with implications beyond spectroscopy for broader knowledge-enhanced scientific analysis.

title: Machine learning-assisted modular triple-signal ratiometric ECL biosensor for multi-Alzheimer's biomarkers detection.
abstract: Triple-signal ratiometric electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensors exhibit superior multidimensional error correction capabilities compared to dual-signal systems. However, current design strategies are constrained by the lack of established criteria for ratiometric signal selection and limited adaptability to multiple targets and detection modes, which highlights the urgent demand for more versatile design strategies. Herein, a modular triple-signal ratiometric ECL biosensor was fabricated. Integrated with machine learning (ML) algorithms, it enabled accurate identification and quantification of different Tau protein, successfully distinguishing Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients from healthy controls and comorbidity populations. The biosensor incorporated graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4), luminol, and Ru(bpy)32+ as luminophores, generating multiple potential-resolved ECL signals at both cathodic and anodic potentials. Specifically, both g-C3N4 and luminol utilized H2O2 as the co-reactant, exhibiting ECL emission at -1.5 V and +0.5 V, respectively, whereas Ru(bpy)32+ generated emission at +1.2 V with TPrA as the co-reactant. The distinct coreaction pathways under different potentials ensured that the three emission channels were mutually independent and free from cross-interference. Through a machine learning algorithm based on variable importance in projection scores, nine ratiometric combinations were ranked, and the optimal ratio was independently validated by receiver operating characteristic analysis. This modular biosensor was configured in both signal-on and signal-off modes, and was designed to detect Tau 381 and Tau 441 at the optimal ratio with detection limits of 3.8 and 3.7 fg mL-1, respectively. This modular biosensor overcame case-by-case optimization and provided a versatile platform for multi-target sensing with significant clinical application potential.

title: Multiphase phosgene detection on machine learning-enhanced fluorescent sensor arrays.
abstract: Phosgene is a highly toxic, volatile asphyxiant and a notorious chemical warfare agent, posing severe threats to public safety, environmental security, and industrial operations. The capability for rapid, selective, and ultrasensitive on-site detection of phosgene is therefore critically important. Nevertheless, the coexistence of phosgene in liquid, gaseous, and solid-phase environments imposes substantially different sensing requirements, making universal detection across multiple phases a longstanding challenge. Herein, we report the rational design and synthesis of three donor-acceptor (D-A) fluorescent probes and the construction of a conjugated donor-regulated fluorescent sensor array for comprehensive phosgene sensing. The developed platform enables highly sensitive detection and selective of phosgene across liquid, gas, and solid phases, demonstrating excellent adaptability under diverse detection conditions. The detection limit of BTTANT in the liquid phase was 0.48 μM, in the gas phase 0.88 ppm, and the fluorescence quenching rate in the solid phase was 88.28%. By integrating RGB colorimetric analysis with a smartphone, we achieved portable on-site quantification. Leveraging machine learning to enhance recognition strategies, we performed in-depth analysis of multidimensional response signals to distinguish phosgene from various structurally similar interferents with high precision. This study established an integrated fluorescence sensing-intelligent recognition detection platform, providing a significant impetus for the rapid, accurate, and in-situ monitoring of phosgene in complex environments.

title: Impact of dataset partitioning on the reliability of SERS-machine learning models for antimicrobial resistance classification.
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global health challenge and motivates the development of rapid analytical approaches for characterizing clinical bacterial isolates. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), combined with machine learning (ML), has emerged as a promising approach for label-free spectral classification of bacterial isolates. However, the field lacks methodological consensus on how hierarchical spectral datasets should be structured, standardized, and partitioned for reliable model evaluation. This gap has led to widespread data leakage and inflated performance reports in SERS-AI studies. Here, we present a systematic benchmarking framework based on 15,000 SERS spectra acquired from 15 clinical Staphylococcus aureus isolates representing distinct resistance phenotypes (MRSA, ERSA, and SSA), evaluating twelve data-partitioning strategies across five machine learning models and three feature selection or dimensionality-reduction methods. Our results show that spectrum-level splits consistently overestimate classification accuracy due to non-independent samples, whereas isolate- or subject-level partitioning provides more realistic estimates of model generalizability. Among the evaluated models, random forest combined with Boruta feature selection produced consistently robust and interpretable performance. Overall, model performance depended more strongly on dataset organization and partitioning strategy than on the choice of machine learning algorithm.

title: Dual-channel CNN fusion of raw and preprocessed serum Raman spectra for robust echinococcosis screening.
abstract: Serum Raman spectroscopy provides label-free molecular fingerprints for bioanalytical screening, but conventional models often rely on a single preprocessing pipeline. Because preprocessing can alter spectral distributions and attenuate information retained in raw spectra, this study developed a dual-channel fusion strategy for echinococcosis screening. We analyzed 573 serum samples from hepatic echinococcosis (HE), liver cirrhosis (LC), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and normal controls (NC); 458 formed the development set and 115 were reserved for held-out testing. We developed a dual-channel convolutional neural network (DCNN) that fused complementary features from raw and preprocessed Raman spectra. Eight preprocessing pipelines and three fusion strategies were evaluated using identical stratified five-fold splits within the development set, and the configuration with the highest mean five-fold accuracy was fixed before held-out testing. The selected fusion strategy was then assessed across all eight pipelines against single-channel models. Under the locked configuration, the DCNN achieved 94.98% ± 1.62% mean accuracy, compared with 89.95% ± 4.36% for the preprocessed-spectrum CNN (P-CNN) and 88.42% ± 2.66% for the raw-spectrum CNN (R-CNN). Held-out accuracies were 95.65% for DCNN, 91.30% for P-CNN, and 89.57% for R-CNN. For binary screening, a DCNN trained on the development set achieved 96.52% accuracy on the held-out set, whereas the dot immunogold filtration assay (DIGFA) yielded 88.70% on the same samples. Feature-level fusion improved the use of complementary spectral information and reduced dependence on a single preprocessing pipeline. This strategy provides a robust framework for rapid, label-free serum Raman screening of echinococcosis.

title: Analytical characterisation of yeast cell walls by lectin-binding flow cytometry and extraction-based polysaccharide analysis.
abstract: Accurate profiling of yeast cell-wall polysaccharides (PS) remains analytically challenging because different methods interrogate different levels of cell-wall organisation. In this study, lectin-binding flow cytometry and extraction-based chemical analysis were comparatively evaluated across 10 representative yeast strains. Flow cytometry revealed marked strain-dependent variation in forward scatter (FSC), side scatter (SSC), and median of lectin fluorescence intensity (MFI), whereas extraction-based analysis showed substantial differences in PS yield, monosaccharide composition, and molecular weight distribution. Using lg-transformed data, Pearson correlation and partial least squares regression (PLSR) analyses showed that FSC and SSC were strongly associated with cell-normalised extractable mannose content (r = 0.89 and 0.88, respectively) and contributed most to its prediction. By contrast, MFI was more strongly related to the mannose to glucose molar ratio (r = 0.90) than to extractable mannose content (r = 0.70), providing strain-specific biochemical information. These findings demonstrate that flow cytometry and extraction-based analysis are complementary approaches. Scatter-based parameters mainly reflect absolute PS abundance associated with cell size, whereas MFI rapidly reflects surface lectin-binding characteristics and PS composition. The combined use of both methods therefore provides a more complete framework for yeast cell-wall characterisation.

title: Machine-learning-enhanced Optical Photothermal infrared (O-PTIR) spectroscopy for rapid simultaneous identification of multiple metabolites to monitor biotransformations: proof of concept on Brewer's spent grain (BSG).
abstract: Monitoring fermentation in chemically complex matrices remains analytically challenging because multiple metabolites evolve simultaneously. Conventional assays are targeted and sequential, and only partial annotation is often available in real samples. In this study, we present a masked multi-label analytical workflow combining optical photothermal infrared spectroscopy (O-PTIR) with a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) for rapid screening of brewer's spent grain fermentations. The methodology couples a library of standard compound spectra with transfer learning on partially labelled fermentation spectra, while masked optimisation avoids penalising unannotated classes during fine-tuning. A library of ten reference compounds and their mixtures was first used to train the model, which was then adapted to fermented samples using qualitative labels for starch, glucose, lactic acid and kojic acid. Supernatants from non-inoculated, separated and sequential bacterial/fungal fermentations were analysed after minimal sample preparation. The pretrained model showed excellent internal validation on the standard library. The fine-tuned 1D-CNN retained high discriminative performance (macro-F1 = 0,950). Benchmarking against one-vs-rest PLS-DA and SVM models using the same held-out BSG validation split showed that the nonlinear models outperformed the linear chemometric baseline. Predicted temporal profiles were consistent with assay-derived phase transitions, notably glucose depletion and lactic acid accumulation during the bacterial stage, followed by starch disappearance and kojic acid appearance during the fungal stage. These results support the use of multi-label O-PTIR workflow to provide rapid and label-free identification of key metabolic phases in partially labelled, heterogeneous matrices, and highlight its potential as a transferable analytical strategy for bioprocess monitoring.

title: A self-calibrating porphyrin-based optofluidic system with edge-deployable chemometrics for online fluoride monitoring.
abstract: In this work, we report a self-calibrating two-channel flow system for a porphyrin-molecule-based optical sensor for the quantification of fluoride (F-) in drinking water, with online monitoring capabilities. The mechanism employs absorbance-based detection of fluoride ion (F-) using 5, 10, 15, 20-Tetraphenyl-21H, 23H-porphine iron(III) chloride (FeTPP) as the sensing probe. The absorbance spectrum of FeTPP was recorded for fluoride ions (F-) in the presence of various interferents including chloride (Cl-), bromide (Br-), iodide (I-), nitrate (NO3-), sulfate (SO42-), phosphate (PO43-), sulfite (SO32-), bisulfide (HS-), azide (N3-) and acetate (CH3COO-) to assess its applicability for real-time detection. Statistical analysis, in conjunction with a multivariate prediction model, has been implemented to estimate the sensitivity and predictive efficiency of the porphyrin sensor. The prediction model showed promising results with a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9983 ± 0.0009 and mean squared error (MSE) of 0.0018 ± 0.0068 in the absence of interferences, and R2 of 0.9928 ± 0.0018 and MSE of 0.0472 ± 0.0422 in the presence of interferences. The effect of environmental parameters such as pH and temperature was also studied to develop a compensated prediction model that yielded a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9867 ± 0.0039 and MSE 0.0590 ± 0.0718. Furthermore, an online fluoride monitoring system has been designed, which includes a flow system with two parallel channels for the chemosensor and the water sample, a compact optical detector unit with an integrated LED and lens assembly, a microcontroller, and a display unit for data acquisition and user interface. The edge-deployed chemometrics, which included a multivariate prediction model, was configured in the microcontroller to predict the fluoride concentration in water. The proposed system showed congruence with recorded absorbance data for the fluoride concentration in a range from 0.1 to 10 ppm. The efficiency of the sensor was also effectively demonstrated for real water samples spiked with fluoride ions. These encouraging findings provide a firm foundation for the implementation of practical field applications in water quality sensing.

title: Machine learning-assisted robust identification of kanamycin under acidic fluctuations using a self-regulated nanoconfined sensor.
abstract: The ultrasensitive detection of kanamycin is important for acidic-condition analytical sensing. However, pH variations in acidic samples often trigger significant background interference, leading to false positive or negative results. In this study, a machine learning-assisted dual-probe nanoconfined sensor (KBA&C4/SiNWs/GMP) was developed for the precise identification of kanamycin under acidic fluctuations. By co-functionalizing a glass micropipette (GMP) filled with silica nanowires (SiNWs) with a kanamycin-binding aptamer (KBA) and a proton-responsive DNA strand (C4 DNA), the sensing interface integrates target recognition with pH-responsive interfacial regulation. To enhance recognition reliability, machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), were employed to classify the ionic current responses. The machine learning models accurately classified concentration-dependent ionic current responses despite signal variations caused by acidity fluctuations, enabling the sensor to maintain a low limit of detection (7.31 fM) and a high classification accuracy (94.17%) in acidic matrices. This work provides a promising strategy for reliable kanamycin detection in acidic and complex sample environments.

title: Color image analysis and machine learning for classification and flavonoid-equivalent prediction of Citri ReticulataePericarpium.
abstract: Citri Reticulatae Pericarpium (CRP) authentication and flavonoid-related quality evaluation commonly rely on chromatographic or spectroscopic techniques, which are accurate but require specialized instrumentation. This study aims to develop a standardized colorimetric image-based machine-learning workflow for rapid CRP origin-aging classification and flavonoid-equivalent prediction. Representative flavonoid monomers were used to compare chromogenic responses in aluminum chloride and sodium nitrite-aluminum nitrate systems. CRP samples were analyzed using standardized image acquisition, color reference normalization, fixed ROI extraction, engineered RGB descriptors, and inverse sRGB gamma correction for regression modeling. For CRP classification, a 480-record model-development set and a 120-record independent held-out validation set were constructed at the image-group level. Through the two chromogenic systems, RF classifier achieved held-out accuracies of 0.9500, 0.9917, and 0.9500 for geographical-origin, aging-year, and combined origin-aging classification, respectively. For flavonoid-equivalent prediction, gamma correction improved the RF external validation R2 from 0.9502 to 0.9789 and reduced the external RMSE from 5.4186 to 3.5231. Spike-recovery values were 104.27 % ± 8.94 %, 102.07 % ± 6.36 %, and 96.74 % ± 6.45 % at the 200, 400, and 800 μg/mL addition levels, respectively. The proposed workflow integrates chromogenic reaction, standardized image acquisition, color feature extraction, gamma correction, and machine learning into a low-cost analytical strategy for CRP authentication. The results indicate that the method can serve as a useful tool for rapid and efficient quality evaluation for CRP.

title: Machine learning-assisted sensor array based on single trimetallic nanozyme with multienzyme-like activities for rapid and intelligent identification of multiple metal ions.
abstract: The concurrent detection and differentiation of multiple heavy metal ions is critical for water quality surveillance, but it continues to pose a significant technical challenge. Herein, this study designed a machine learning-assisted sensor array based on single trimetallic nanozyme (PVP-PtCuAu NCs) with multienzyme-like activities for rapid and intelligent identification of multiple metal ions (Pb2+, Ag+, As3+, Cu2+ and Hg2+). Wherein, the trimetallic nanozyme (PVP-PtCuAu NCs) exhibited good multienzyme-mimicking activities, including peroxidase-like, oxidase-like and laccase-like catalytic properties. Notably, different metal ions could effectively regulate the three enzyme-like activities of PVP-PtCuAu NCs, generating diverse cross-reaction optical response patterns. On this basis, a three-channel colorimetric sensor array based on PVP-PtCuAu NCs nanozyme was constructed, enabling the rapid and accurate identification of five metal ions and their mixtures. Furthermore, to enhance analytical performance, machine learning algorithms were employed to integrate with the nanozyme sensor array for processing the three-channel response data, achieving highly reliable qualitative classification and quantitative prediction of five metal ions, which also demonstrated satisfactory applicability in real water samples. Overall, this study presents a facile and efficient approach for the rapid discrimination of multiple metal ions in environmental waters, offering broad application prospects for environmental monitoring and water quality assessment.

title: UCT-LMIR: A standard-free unsupervised calibration transfer method without model recalibration.
abstract: Cross-instrument spectral variations in intensity, baseline, and noise structure severely undermine the transferability of multivariate calibration models, limiting their practical deployment across spectroscopic platforms. Existing calibration transfer methods typically rely on standard samples, target domain reference labels, or model recalibration, all of which incur substantial experimental or computational costs. This work proposes unsupervised calibration transfer via likelihood maximization inverse regression (UCT-LMIR), which simultaneously eliminates the need for standard samples, target domain reference labels, and model recalibration. UCT-LMIR constructs an error covariance model within a latent space and performs prediction by maximizing the likelihood of a target spectrum under the learned error structure. An optional covariance compensation term accounts for the additional dispersion induced by cross-domain spectral discrepancies, enabling the method to accommodate varying degrees of instrumental mismatch. Validation on three spectroscopic datasets with distinct distributional characteristics showed that UCT-LMIR outperformed representative unsupervised calibration transfer methods in the majority of transfer tasks, with particularly pronounced improvements under large inter-instrument distribution shifts where competing methods often failed. UCT-LMIR provides a standard-free and unsupervised calibration transfer strategy that does not require model recalibration. By combining physical interpretability with ease of implementation, it offers a practical and robust solution for calibration transfer in real-world spectroscopic applications.

title: Machine learning-assisted dual-mode immunochromatographic detection of pentachlorophenol via oriented antibody-functionalized AFIrTPs nanoprobes.
abstract: Pentachlorophenol (PCP), a human carcinogen, is widely detected in human biosamples, despite being banned in aquaculture, continues to show high detection frequencies in aquatic products according to regulatory reports. Therefore, there is an urgent need for reliable on-site testing methods. Immunochromatographic assay (ICA) are promising, but conventional ICA suffers from antibody deactivation and unstable single-signal outputs in complex matrices. Herein, we reported a self-assembly method to fabricate tannic acid (TA)-mediated sea urchin-like Au/Fe/Ir trimetallic nanoparticles (AFIrTPs) that overcome these challenges. TA created a biofriendly interface that preserved Abs activity, while Fe3+ coordinated with the histidine-rich Fc domains to orient Abs, simplifying immobilization. Benefiting from the strong colorimetric response and efficient photothermal conversion of AFIrTPs, dual-mode ICA achieved detection limits of 3.47 pg/mL (colorimetric) and 2.19 pg/mL (photothermal). To facilitate PCP monitoring, a K-nearest neighbors algorithm enabled accurate classification and quantification of PCP, achieving a 99.3% classification accuracy. The assay shows satisfactory specificity and reliability, offering a promising platform for PCP on-site monitoring.

title: Imbalance-aware spectral classification via logit-label adjustment and multi-expert mutual learning.
abstract: The integration of deep learning with molecular vibrational spectroscopy has been widely investigated in domains such as disease diagnosis and food safety. However, existing spectral recognition methods assume a balanced class distribution in the training set, where each class contains an equal number of samples. In real-world scenarios, such as rare disease diagnosis, class imbalance is far more common, posing significant challenges to model generalization. To tackle this issue, we propose Spec-ImC, a novel approach specifically designed to address class imbalance in spectral classification and better align with practical application needs. Specifically, we introduce a Logit-Label Adjustment (LLA) strategy, which recalibrates both logits and labels to mitigate the bias in decision boundaries toward many-shot classes. To further enhance model robustness, we propose a Cosine-Annealed Data Augmentation (CADA) strategy together with a novel Consistency Regularization (CR) technique, which stabilizes gradient updates even under strong data augmentation. Furthermore, we develop a Multi-Expert Mutual Learning (MEML) mechanism, enabling multiple expert models to exchange knowledge, thereby fostering feature diversity and boosting recognition performance, particularly for few-shot classes. Extensive experiments on two bacterial spectral datasets, namely Bacterial ID and Bacterial Stain, as well as one cancer spectral dataset, namely Cancer, demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods under various simulated imbalance scenarios, indicating its effectiveness and potential applicability to class-imbalanced spectral analysis tasks. The proposed framework effectively mitigates the adverse effects of class imbalance in spectral classification and provides a robust solution for molecular vibrational spectroscopy applications with long-tailed data distributions. Its superior performance and generalizability indicate strong potential for real-world spectral analysis tasks, particularly in applications involving rare categories and limited training samples.

title: Imidazole derivative-regulated Cu-MOF nanozyme sensor array integrating machine learning for flavonoids detection and soy milk traceability.
abstract: Flavonoids are important natural bioactive compounds with remarkable health benefits, requiring rapid and accurate detection for food nutrition assessment and quality control. However, it remains challenging to simultaneously discriminate multiple flavonoids in complex matrices. Taking inspiration from the tunable structures of MOF-based nanozymes and the ability of sensor arrays to simultaneously detect multiple substances, we herein propose an innovative four-channel colorimetric sensor array for flavonoid identification. Four copper-based MOF nanozymes (Cu-ImC2N, Cu-ImC2, Cu-ImCl2, Cu-ImPh) were synthesized with different imidazole derivatives as ligands, showing significant differences in their peroxidase-like activities. Exploiting their specific catalytic activity variations at pH 6.0 and 6.5, the two most active nanozymes (Cu-ImC2N and Cu-ImC2) were strategically selected to construct the array. Upon processing the array data with linear discriminant analysis (LDA), the array achieved 100% accurate discrimination and quantitative detection of seven flavonoids, with limits of detection (LODs) ranging from 0.039 to 0.982 μM. Furthermore, comparisons of concentration-independent models built with multiple machine learning algorithms showed that the K-nearest neighbors (KNN) method outperformed LDA, effectively reducing interference from concentration variations. The sensor array was successfully applied to the analysis of commercial soy milk, reliably differentiating products from different brands and bean sources (e.g., soybean and mung bean). This strategy surpasses traditional single-analyte methods and holds substantial practical potential for the rapid on-site detection of complex food systems.

title: Development of a SERS-based diagnostic tool for infectious vaginitis via intelligent analysis of vaginal fluid spectra.
abstract: Vaginal infections, including bacterial vaginosis (BV), vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC), and trichomoniasis (TV), are common gynecologic disorders in reproductive age women. Accurate differential diagnosis remains challenging due to overlapping symptoms and limitations of conventional microscopy and biochemical assays. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) provides label-free molecular fingerprints of complex biological fluids and may support automated classification when combined with machine learning. The problem addressed here is the lack of a label-free analytical strategy for patient-level discrimination of healthy controls (HC), BV, VVC, and TV using vaginal fluid samples. SERS spectra were acquired from vaginal fluid samples using citrate-reduced silver nanoparticles (AgNPs). A total of 170 participants were enrolled, with one vaginal secretion sample collected from each participant. Among these samples, 135 samples (HC = 40, BV = 40, VVC = 40, TV = 15) were used for model construction and 35 independent samples (HC = 10, BV = 10, VVC = 10, TV = 5) were used for independent blind validation. Although the average SERS spectra of HC, BV, and VVC showed substantial overlap, spectral deconvolution revealed subtle class-related features. Thirteen machine-learning and deep-learning models were evaluated using a patient-wise strategy. The one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1DCNN) achieved the most balanced performance, with an internal hold-out patient-level accuracy of 80.0% and a macro-AUC of 0.92. Independent blind validation correctly classified 31 of 35 participants, corresponding to an external patient-level accuracy of 88.6%. This study establishes a patient-wise SERS and machine-learning framework for four-class discrimination of HC, BV, VVC, and TV. Its novelty lies in combining vaginal-secretion SERS fingerprints, patient-level data splitting, majority-vote classification, and independent blind validation. This label-free and automated framework may provide an objective complement to conventional microscopic and biochemical testing in future diagnostic workflows.

title: Multimodal serum vibrational spectroscopy with availability-aware deep learning for prediction of pathological complete response in breast cancer.
abstract: Accurate assessment of pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy is clinically important in breast cancer, yet reliable preoperative evaluation remains challenging. Serum vibrational spectroscopy provides a label-free and minimally invasive approach for capturing biochemical variation associated with subsequent treatment response in biofluids. However, clinical application is often constrained by limited sample size, class imbalance, and incomplete acquisition of multimodal spectral data. To address these constraints, we developed an availability-aware multimodal spectroscopy and mask-aware learning framework for serum pCR prediction, combining 532 nm Raman, 785 nm surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra with CGAN-based augmentation and adaptive multimodal fusion. A conditional generative adversarial network (CGAN) was used to generate synthetic spectra for training augmentation, while MRAM-Net adaptively fused available spectral representations without spectral imputation. Using repeated patient-level cross-validation, the framework achieved an AUC of 94.2% when all modalities were available and maintained robust performance when one modality was unavailable (AUC >88%). In the independent validation cohort, the locked model achieved an AUC of 95.8% and an accuracy of 92.3% using the development threshold. These results indicate that the availability-aware framework can maintain stable performance under clinical data constraints. The proposed framework provides a practical strategy for treatment response assessment in breast cancer and a methodological basis for analyzing incomplete multimodal vibrational spectroscopy datasets in translational applications.

title: Applications of AI-assisted interpreter Raman spectroscopy platform for rapid and accurate cefotaxime-resistant Escherichia coli classification.
abstract: The emergence of cefotaxime resistance in Escherichia coli (E. coli) poses a significant challenge in clinical practice, driving a demand for rapid diagnostics. Here, we introduce a label-free approach combining Raman spectroscopy with deep learning to rapidly distinguish between cefotaxime-resistant and susceptible E. coli strains. Using clinically isolated samples, we developed classification models based on AlexNet, ResNet, and PCA-LDA algorithms. Evaluation on the internal test set showed that the AlexNet model achieved superior performance, with an accuracy of 88.13% and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.944. ResNet and PCA-LDA attained accuracies of 81.25% and 78.34%, respectively, with AUC values above 0.85, highlighting the advantage of deep learning in Raman-based resistance identification. To interpret the decision mechanism, we integrated Binary Stochastic Filtering (BSF) with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis, identifying discriminative spectral features (tentatively assigned to candidate biomolecules such as phenylalanine, tryptophan, and nucleic acids) associated with E. coli linked to cefotaxime resistance. Especially, an exploratory 1D Transformer model achieved 94.38% accuracy with 8% gain and an AUC of 0.991 with 0.07 gain for Raman spectral classification, through introducing global feature modeling. In conclusion, this work offers a promising tool for rapid resistance screening (<0.5 h), while leveraging interpretable AI to reveal candidate spectral biomarkers, thereby aiding in elucidating resistance mechanisms and guiding targeted therapy.

title: Can we predict drug permeability class in intestinal epithelial cells using in situ live-cell ATR-FTIR spectroscopy?
abstract: Membrane permeability plays a vital role in oral drug absorption and is one of the important reasons for attrition of promising drug candidates in early-stage drug discovery. Conventional in vitro permeability assays and metabolomics-based approaches are informative but are often destructive, labor-intensive, costly and limited to endpoint measurements. Here, we report a live-cell attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy platform for label-free, cost-effective, non-destructive monitoring of biochemical responses in Caco-2 cells following exposure to model drugs spanning multiple Biopharmaceutics Classification System (BCS) classes. IR spectra in the biochemical fingerprint region (1800-950 cm-1) were then analysed using principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering. Distinct spectral signatures were observed for highly permeable versus poorly permeable compounds, with discriminatory features dominated by protein (amide I/II), lipid and phosphate-associated bands. Drugs that highly permeate through membranes left a clearly different spectral trail compared to those that do not. Importantly, chemometric separation was achieved within the early hours of exposure, demonstrating the potential of live-cell ATR-FTIR spectroscopy as a rapid, low-cost and non-destructive complement to conventional permeability screening assays. These findings support the use of in situ live-cell ATR-FTIR spectroscopy as a promising approach for predicting drug permeability class in intestinal epithelial cells during early drug discovery.

title: Beyond trial-and-error: Fast in silico optimization of electromembrane extraction methods based on machine learning and a desktop app.
abstract: Electromembrane extraction (EME) is a rapid and solvent-efficient sample preparation technique, yet method development remains highly empirical and time-consuming, as extraction recovery depends on complex relationships between analyte properties and operational parameters. Generic EME methods provide useful starting points but cannot account for the chemical diversity encountered in real applications, and no tools currently exist to predict extraction performance or guide optimization. Here, we present the first data-driven framework for quantitative prediction and in silico optimization of EME. Using commercial instrumentation and central composite designs, the effects of sample pH, voltage, and time were systematically explored across five generic supported liquid membranes, for 182 chemically diverse analytes in human plasma. The resulting dataset was used to develop neural network models that combine molecular descriptors with experimental conditions to estimate extraction recoveries. The models showed strong predictive performance (R2test = 0.86-0.97; mean absolute error = 6.3-9.8% for recoveries >10%). To enable practical application, we developed EME Predictor (available at https://github.com/fredehan/EME-Predictor), a freely available desktop tool for predicting recoveries of new analytes and optimizing extraction parameters. External validation using a set of 47 compounds from forensic toxicology confirmed good model generalization, including for previously unseen compounds. This work demonstrates how data-driven modelling can transform EME method development from trial-and-error to rational optimization. By combining machine learning with a practical desktop application, the proposed framework improves the efficiency, accessibility, and broader adoption of EME for analytical method development.

title: Miniaturized mass spectrometry integrated with ambient ionization sources: a review of system-level advances and emerging analytical applications.
